tools.name: list_components
tools.description: List the shipped @recipebooq/ui components — slug, purpose, category, and which are real iOS system controls vs. our own glass. Call this first; it is cheap. Optionally filter by category or tech.

tools.name: get_component
tools.description: Everything needed to write a correct call site for one component: props with types, defaults and value domains, platform applicability, dependencies — and the runtime rules that apply to it. Always read the rules; getting props right and rules wrong still ships a blank screen.

tools.name: find_component
tools.description: Describe a UI need in plain language and get ranked components — including an explicit answer when this catalog deliberately does NOT ship something and you should use the OS's own control instead. Call this before building any UI control by hand.

tools.name: get_rules
tools.description: The runtime rules for this catalog — the mistakes that make native Liquid Glass render blank with no warning, no error and no red box. Pass a slug to scope them to one component. Read these before writing animation or layout code against any glass component.

tools.name: get_provider_tree
tools.description: The exact app-root provider nesting these components require, in the order that works. Getting this wrong fails at runtime, not at compile time. Optionally pass the components you are using to see which providers they each need.

tools.name: get_theme_tokens
tools.description: The theme system: which hooks to call, and the spacing, radius and typography scales. Reference token names rather than hex values so a retheme propagates.

tools.name: check_snippet
tools.description: Paste TSX that uses these components and get back the glass-safety problems in it — the animated opacity, the flex:1 collapse, the clipped lens, the conditional mount. Read-only: it never touches your repo. A heuristic text scan, not a structural guarantee.

tools.name: emit_app
tools.description: PAID. Turn a recipebooq canvas into a working app: navigation, providers, tab bar, screens and the components they need. Returns a recipe — the exact files with their target paths, the dependency install line, and ordered steps — to apply to the current project. Files marked `skeleton` or `component

tools.description: PAID. Add one new screen to an app that was already exported: the screen file, the route that mounts it, the exact line to register it, and how to navigate to it. tools.name: update_components
tools.description: PAID. Tell the customer what has changed in their recipebooq files since they exported, and hand back only what moved. tools.name: verify_app
tools.description: PAID. Check that an emitted app was actually applied correctly, before building it. tools.name: get_step
tools.description: FREE. Expand one step of an emit_app recipe: the full instruction, why it matters, how to know it worked, and what to do when it did not. emit_app returns steps in short form to stay inside the response budget — call this before any step you are not completely sure about. tools.name: emit_screen
tools.description: PAID. Turn one composed screen into a real TSX file you can drop into an app you already have — your navigator, your routes. Returns the complete file inline, the components to install first, and how to mount it. Use emit_app instead when the customer wants a whole app with navigation and a tab bar.
